title: Etale localization of algebraic-space strict transforms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Closed and open immersions are representable and have the indicated property on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Modules are on small etale ringed sites, with quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is of finite type if etale locally finitely generated; it is of finite presentation if etale locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to M\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. For a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$, write $p:T'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, obtained by etale descent of scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Its exceptional effective Cartier divisor $E$ has ideal locally generated by a non-zero-divisor $t$. For $f:X\to T$, the module strict transform of $M$ is $M'=q^*M/\{m:t^a m=0\text{ for some }a\geq0\}$ on $X\times_TT'$, where $q$ is the projection to $X$. The space strict transform is the closed subspace cut out by this torsion ideal for $M=\mathcal O_X$. These definitions retain the centre $\mathcal K$. Let $f:X\to T$ be any morphism, denote its space strict transform by $X\prime$, and let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal. Let $A,W$ be schemes in a commuting square $W\to X$, $A\to T$, $W\to A$, with both horizontal maps etale. Let $A'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K\mathcal O_A}A$. Then $A'\cong A\times_TT'$ over $A$ and $T'$, the maps $A'\to T'$ and $W\times_A A'\to X\times_TT'$ are etale, and the strict transform $W'$ is canonically $X'\times_X W$. For every quasi-coherent $M$ on $X$, restriction of $M'$ to $W\times_A A'$ is canonically the module strict transform of $M|_W$ relative to $A'\to A$, compatibly with the quotient maps from the pulled-back modules. If $W\to X\times_TA$ and $A\to T$ are surjective, then the induced maps from the transformed charts are also surjective. No flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$ or $M$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_TT'$ and $Y_W=W\times_AA'$. The covering-calculus lemma applied to $\{A\to T,\mathrm{id}_T\}$ says its members are flat. Hence the blowup flat-base-change statement gives $A'\simeq A\times_TT'$ in the extended ideal $\mathcal K\mathcal O_A$. It identifies $A'\to T'$ with the base change of $A\to T$. Associativity gives $Y_W\simeq W\times_XY$, so $h:Y_W\to Y$ is the base change of $W\to X$. The fibre-product covering lemma applied to each étale map together with the identity gives that both base changes are étale, without surjectivity hypotheses. The exceptional ideal on $A'$ is the extension of that on $T'$: both are the image of the pullback of $\mathcal K$ in $\mathcal O_{A'}$. Thus their further pullbacks to $Y_W$ agree.

source.place: Tag 0863, proof of (1), using Tag 085S (flat base change for blowups) and the base-change stability of étale maps

proof.text: Let $H=q^*M$ on $Y$. The module-restriction comparison identifies $h^*H$ with $q_W^*(M|_W)$, where $q_W:Y_W\to W$; this comparison uses the two paths around the cartesian square $Y_W\to Y$, $W\to X$ and keeps the restricted module sections. It also identifies $h^*$ with restriction to the localized étale site. Denote by $K\subset H$ the exceptional power-torsion subsheaf. On any étale scheme test $V\to Y_W$ lying in a region with exceptional equation $t$, both $K|_{Y_W}$ and the exceptional torsion subsheaf of $H|_{Y_W}$ consist locally of precisely the same sections $m$ satisfying $t^am=0$ for some $a$. The equation on this test is literally the pullback of $t$ by step 1. Thus the two subsheaves coincide, with their inclusions into $H|_{Y_W}$. Restriction preserves the quotient: the quotient sheaf is the sheafification of the sectionwise quotient, and its local representatives and equality after a covering are unchanged on the localized site. Consequently $M'|_{Y_W}\simeq q_W^*(M|_W)/K_W$, preserving every class of a local section and therefore the quotient maps. This proves the module clause directly; no flatness of $f$ or $M$ has entered.

proof.text: Apply step 2 with $M=\mathcal O_X$. Pullback of this module is the structure sheaf. The identification of torsion subsheaves is also an identification of ideals: on local sections it keeps the same functions and multiplication, and its quotient sends a function class to that same function class. On affine tests this is the equality of rings $B\otimes_R(R/I)\simeq B/IB$, $b\otimes\bar r\mapsto\overline{br}$, with inverse $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Hence the subspace defined by the restricted torsion ideal is the pullback of $X'\subset Y$, including its closed-subspace structure. It is $X'\times_Y Y_W\simeq X'\times_XW$, which proves the space clause.

source.place: Tag 0863, proof of (2): apply (3) to F=O_X

proof.text: Assume the stated covering hypotheses: $A\to T$ and $W\to X\times_TA$ are surjective. Base change of the first, by the fibre-product covering lemma, makes $X\times_TA\to X$ surjective. Composing with the second makes $W\to X$ surjective: any point of $X$ has a preimage in $X\times_TA$, and that point has a preimage in $W$. The original horizontal map $W\to X$ is already étale. Apply the covering lemma to the singleton families $\{W\to X\}$ and $\{A\to T\}$ and base change along $Y\to X$ and $T'\to T$. Step 1 identifies these base changes with $Y_W\to Y$ and $A'\to T'$, proving their surjectivity. A further base change along $X'\to Y$ gives the transformed chart cover $W'\simeq X'\times_XW\to X'$.
